cards.f: Where to plot cumulative frequency points
cards.b: At the upper class boundary. Start the curve at (lowest boundary, 0).

cards.f: Reading quartiles from a cumulative frequency graph
cards.b: Q₁ at n/4, median at n/2, Q₃ at 3n/4 (n = total frequency). Read across, then down to the value.
Read at (p/100) × n on the cumulative frequency axis.
Lower boundary + ((n/2 − cf before class) ÷ class frequency) × class width.

cards.f: Five values in a box plot
cards.b: Minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, maximum.
Box from Q₁ to Q₃ with a line at the median. Whiskers to the minimum and maximum. Use a ruler and labelled scale.
Lower: Q₁ − 1.5 × IQR. Upper: Q₃ + 1.5 × IQR. Values outside are outliers.
Show the limit calculation, then conclude clearly, e.g. 'so 58 is an outlier'. Use 1.5 × IQR, not the range.
Long tail to the right. Q₃ − Q₂ > Q₂ − Q₁ and mean > median > mode.
Long tail to the left. Q₃ − Q₂ < Q₂ − Q₁ and mean < median < mode.
Q₃ − Q₂ = Q₂ − Q₁ and mean = median = mode.
Incomes: most people earn moderate amounts, a few earn a lot.
At least two comparisons in context with values: location (median), spread (IQR), and skew if asked.

short.q: Masses of 50 parcels: 0 < m ≤ 20 has 5, 20 < m ≤ 40 has 15, 40 < m ≤ 60 has 20, 60 < m ≤ 80 has 10. Complete the cumulative frequencies, then estimate the median and the interquartile range using interpolation. [4]
Q₁ = 22 and Q₃ = 34. The largest value in the data is 60. Show whether 60 is an outlier. [3]
short.model: IQR = 12. Upper limit = 34 + 1.5 × 12 = 52. Since 60 > 52, it is an outlier.

short.q: A distribution has Q₁ = 10, median = 18 and Q₃ = 22. Describe its skewness and justify your answer. [2]
short.model: Negative skew: Q₃ − Q₂ = 4 is less than Q₂ − Q₁ = 8.

short.q: A cumulative frequency graph for 150 students shows that 114 scored 60 marks or less. How many scored more than 60, and what percentile is a mark of 60? [2]
short.model: 150 − 114 = 36 students scored more than 60. 114 ÷ 150 = 0.76, so 60 is the 76th percentile.

short.q: Class A has median 52 and IQR 14. Class B has median 47 and IQR 8. Compare the two classes. [2]
short.model: A's median is higher (52 vs 47), so A generally scored higher. B's IQR is smaller (8 vs 14), so B's marks were more consistent.
